newsitem.title: ALBANIA: ALBANIAN PM TURNS TO WEST IN DEEPENING CRISIS.
newsitem.headline: ALBANIAN PM TURNS TO WEST IN DEEPENING CRISIS.

text.p: Albania's government warned of "unforeseen consequences" on Tuesday in a deepening political crisis and said Prime Minister Bashkim Fino had appealed to the West for help.
Despite marathon talks on Monday, Fino failed to persuade most parties to end a threatened boycott of elections in the volatile Balkan country.

"Although the debate continued all Monday, it failed not only to bring compromise or come near to compromise, but on the contrary took Albania to the edge of a deeper crisis with unforeseen consequences," Fino's office said in a statement.
Italy, leader of a multinational troop force safeguarding humanitarian aid, called on all political groups to make concessions.
"The next 24 hours are very important for the future of Albania," Italian Defence Minister Beniamino Andreatta told reporters in Rome.

Fino's spokesman said the premier had late on Monday contacted Italian Prime Minister Romani Prodi, European envoy Franz Vranitzky and U.S. Assistant Secretary of State for European and Canadian Affairs John Kornblum.

"He (Fino) is waiting for reactions from the international community on what Vranitzky and the others will say today, what they are to do, will they come or not and on what basis further steps will be taken," the spokesman said.

Western countries have warned they may cut aid to Albania unless free and fair elections are held to restore stability. Italy has said that, without elections, the troop force guarding aid supplies may withdraw.
Former communist Albania plunged into anarchy and violence in February and March after thousands of people were left penniless by the collapse of pyramid investment schemes.
Violence has subsided markedly in recent weeks but some regions remain lawless. Nine people have been reported killed in gunfire since Sunday.
In a separate incident, Greece's foreign ministry said the head bodyguard at its consulate in the southern town of Gjirokaster killed himself accidentally on Tuesday while cleaning his gun.

Rumours abounded that Vranitzky, special envoy of the Organsation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE), would make another troubleshooting mission to Albania although five previous trips have failed to hammer out an accord.
Most parties of Fino's nine-party government say current election laws favour President Sali Berisha and his former ruling Democratic Party and want the laws changed.

Genc Pollo, a senior Democratic Party official, said the parties still disagreed over how many seats should be decided by proportional representation and how many by first-past-the-post majority voting.
"This takes us back to where we were four weeks ago," Pollo said.

The right-wing Democratic Party and its main rival, the Socialists, have been clashing for months over electoral rules. The Democrats favour more majority voting while the Socialists back more proportional representation. REUTER
